state:
Goal `core-router-and-4-more`, stage 2 (feature proofs). Every `Core\Router` member has every feature proof on disk, `signedRoute` included: about, three examples with a `.nvsr` request beside each, an attack with its own `.nvsr`, a bench with `benches/members/core/Router/signedRoute.nvsr`, a perf figure, and a Rust `covers:` test. Its card is rewritten in plain words. `bun nv proofs --verify --group 'Core\Router'` is the check that should now pass.

The attack found a bug, fixed in the same session: `crate::keyring::borrow` now checks the newest key's length itself. Before, `signedRoute` and `$uri->verifySignature` answered the forgery sentence for a 31-byte first key whenever the request had no `_sig` or two, since they refuse that input before the ring walk. Pinned by `borrowing_a_ring_refuses_a_newest_key_of_the_wrong_length_and_nothing_older` in `crates/nvs-stdlib/src/keyring.rs` and `tests/conformance/core/keyring-a-short-first-key-is-refused-before-the-input-is-read.nvst`.

A `.nvsr` request with a valid `_sig` is minted by running a throwaway program that calls `urlSigned` with the same fixed 32-byte key (`"example-key-for-signed-links-001" as bytes`) and `until: null`, and pasting the query into `--QUERY--`.

`Core\Router\Match`'s class card and members, `Core\Script`, `Core\Script\ExitReport` and `Core\Secret` are not started.
